evals.prompt: Our order service synchronously calls pricing over JSON REST. Checkout has a 300 ms p95 end-to-end objective; traces show pricing at 180 ms p95 but do not separate application time from transport. The call is unary, and an order cannot be priced without its response. Should we move to gRPC? Compare the protocol tradeoff and define timeout behavior.
evals.expected_output: Compare REST and gRPC against the stated 300 ms end-to-end objective without assuming the protocol is the bottleneck: the 180 ms pricing span is not a transport measurement, and this unary flow has no streaming need. REST preserves the existing JSON/HTTP contract and tooling; gRPC offers a typed schema and may reduce call overhead, but adds schema/code-generation and client/proxy compatibility cost. Keep REST if representative tests show it meets the deadline; choose gRPC only if measured protocol/schema benefits justify that cost. Bound the call by the remaining deadline; on timeout, do not create an order at an unknown price, and return a retryable failure rather than waiting or retrying blindly.

assertions.description: Compares valid protocol choices rather than requiring one
Separates protocol cost from the observed service span
Defines the failure outcome for a required price

evals.prompt: We need to push live order status to the customer's browser. The team wants WebSockets.
evals.expected_output: Chooses SSE for a server-push-only flow because it is cheaper and survives proxies better, reserves WebSocket for bidirectional needs, and names the stateful connections, LB affinity, and reconnect protocol costs it would charge.

assertions.description: Picks the one-directional option for a one-directional need
Names the cost of the connection-based option

evals.prompt: A partner wants us to notify them whenever an order ships. What do we build?
evals.expected_output: Specifies an outbound webhook with signature verification, a bounded retry policy with backoff, and an idempotency key, and refuses to treat any of the three as optional.

value: No webhook without signature, retry policy, and idempotency key

evals.prompt: A nightly job calls our billing service once per run to fetch a summary. Someone suggested moving it to gRPC with streaming for consistency with the rest of the stack.
evals.expected_output: Keeps REST for a cold, once-per-night call because the paradigm is chosen per hop from the constraint, and notes that mixing REST at the edge with gRPC internally is normal rather than an inconsistency to fix.

assertions.description: Chooses per hop instead of standardizing for its own sake
Keeps the simpler protocol for a cold path
